cohort: The study participants included mothers with PCOS (n = 101) and mothers without PCOS (n = 204) who had undergone intrauterine insemination, along with their offspring.
finding: The co-occurrence of elevated maternal BMI and PCOS may be associated with an elevated risk of neonatal complications and delivery by caesarean section following IUI.
mod_finding: Maternal BMI was a positive predictor of caesarean section delivery in both PCOS and non-PCOS groups, with a higher adjusted odds ratio found in the PCOS group.
